audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for secret anointing, coup dynamics, watchtower reports, Joram and Ahaziah killings, Naboth-land oracle, Jezebel's presentation and taunt, eunuch participation, trampling, body desecration, and prophetic fulfillment rhetoric.

verses.restored: Elisha the prophet called one of sons of prophets and said to him, Gird your loins, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you come there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, make him rise from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.
Take flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, Thus says YHWH: I have anointed you king over Israel. Then open door, flee, and do not wait.
The young man, servant of prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
He came, and look, commanders of army were sitting. He said, A word I have for you, commander. Jehu said, For which of all of us? He said, For you, commander.
He rose and went into house. He poured oil on his head and said to him, Thus says YHWH Divine of Israel: I have anointed you king over people of YHWH, over Israel.
You shall strike house of Ahab your master, so I may avenge blood of my servants the prophets and blood of all servants of YHWH from hand of Jezebel.
All house of Ahab shall perish; I will cut off from Ahab every male, restrained and released in Israel.
I will make house of Ahab like house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
Dogs shall eat Jezebel in portion of Jezreel, and none shall bury her. Then he opened door and fled.
Jehu went out to servants of his lord. One said to him, Is there peace? Why did this madman come to you? He said to them, You know the man and his talk.
They said, False! Tell us, please. He said, Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, Thus says YHWH: I have anointed you king over Israel.
They hurried, each took his garment and put it under him on bare steps, blew trumpet, and said, Jehu is king!
Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Joram had been guarding Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Aram.
King Joram returned to Jezreel to heal from wounds Arameans struck him when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, If your soul is with me, let no fugitive go out from city to tell in Jezreel.
Jehu rode and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
The watchman stood on tower in Jezreel and saw company of Jehu coming. He said, I see a company. Joram said, Take a rider and send to meet them, and let him say, Is there peace?
The horseman went to meet him and said, Thus says king: Is there peace? Jehu said, What is there to you and peace? Turn behind me. Watchman reported, Messenger reached them and does not return.
He sent a second horseman. He came to them and said, Thus says king: Is there peace? Jehu said, What is there to you and peace? Turn behind me.
Watchman reported, He reached them and does not return; driving is like driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives with madness/fury.
Joram said, Harness. They harnessed his chariot. Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, to meet Jehu; they found him at portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram saw Jehu, he said, Is there peace, Jehu? He said, What peace, while prostitutions/idolatries of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries remain?
Joram turned his hands and fled and said to Ahaziah, Treachery, Ahaziah!
Jehu drew bow with full strength and struck Joram between his arms; arrow went out through his heart, and he sank in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, Lift and throw him into portion of field of Naboth the Jezreelite, for remember, when I and you rode together after Ahab his father, YHWH lifted this burden against him.
Surely I saw yesterday blood of Naboth and blood of his sons, says YHWH, and I will repay you in this portion, says YHWH. Now lift and throw him into portion, according to word of YHWH.
Ahaziah king of Judah saw and fled by way of garden house. Jehu pursued him and said, Strike him also in chariot. They struck him at ascent of Gur by Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him in chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in city of David.
In eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
Jehu came to Jezreel. Jezebel heard; she put paint on her eyes, arranged her head, and looked out through window.
As Jehu entered gate, she said, Is there peace, Zimri, killer of his master?
He lifted his face toward window and said, Who is with me? Who? Two or three eunuchs looked down to him.
He said, Throw her down. They threw her down, and some of her blood splattered on wall and horses, and he trampled her.
He came in, ate and drank, and said, Attend now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is daughter of a king.
They went to bury her, but found no more of her than skull, feet, and palms of hands.
They returned and told him. He said, This is word of YHWH that he spoke by hand of Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In portion of Jezreel dogs shall eat flesh of Jezebel.
Corpse of Jezebel shall be as dung on face of field in portion of Jezreel, so they will not say, This is Jezebel.

translation_notes: Jehu's anointing is secret, hurried, and immediately becomes a military coup. Prophetic commissioning does not remove accountability for methods, targets, or civilian consequences.
The command to destroy Ahab's entire house repeats dynastic-extermination rhetoric and must never justify family killing, inherited guilt, or political purges.
Calling the prophetic messenger a 'madman' reflects contempt toward ecstatic or unusual behavior; it must not be weaponized against mentally ill or neurodivergent people.
Joram is killed while recovering from battle wounds, and Ahaziah is pursued and killed while visiting him. Coup success is not due process.
Naboth's murdered family is invoked as the moral grievance behind Joram's death, but restorative justice cannot be achieved through another unlawful killing.
Jezebel's cosmetics and arranged hair may signal royal dignity, defiance, seduction, or death preparation. They must not support misogynistic readings that blame appearance, sexuality, or femininity.
Jezebel is thrown from a window, trampled, eaten by dogs, and denied burial. This is body desecration and gendered humiliation, not a spiritually satisfying ending.
The eunuchs' role may reflect palace coercion, survival, or alliance with Jehu; the text does not grant access to their motives.
Prophetic-fulfillment language reports the narrator's theology but does not make corpse abuse, misogyny, or coup violence ethically normative.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 9 to justify coups, summary execution, family extermination, misogyny toward Jezebel, mental-health slurs, corpse desecration, or the claim that prophetic authorization removes legal and moral accountability. Keep Naboth's injustice visible without turning vengeance into justice.
